About Figure

Figure Technology Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: FIGR; OPEN: FGRS) is the leading blockchain-native capital marketplace for the origination, funding, sale and trading of tokenized assets. More than 480 partners use its loan origination system and capital marketplace. Collectively, Figure and its partners have originated over $30 billion of loans to date, among other products. The fastest growing components are Figure Connect, its credit marketplace, and Democratized Prime, Figure’s on-chain lend-borrow marketplace. Figure’s ecosystem also includes DART (Digital Asset Registry Technology) for asset custody and lien perfection, and $YLDS, a yield-bearing stablecoin registered with the SEC as a security under the Securities Act of 1933.

Figure is the market leader in real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. The company has received triple-A ratings ratings from S&P and Moody’s on multiple loan securitizations, the first of its kind for blockchain finance.

We’re proud to be recognized as one of Forbes’ Top 50 Fintech Companies and CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Sales Operations Analyst to join our growing team! As Sales Operations Analyst, you’ll support all aspects of the day-to-day Sales function. The role is a mix of direct sales rep support, data integrity, tactical task execution, and task automation. You’ll be highly detail oriented and comfortable getting in the weeds, while always looking for ways to create efficiencies. You’ll join a team of stellar Sales and Marketing Operations analysts and work closely with Sales Representatives, Sales Leaders, Marketing, and cross-functional teams.

What You’ll Do

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for Salesforce and Ops Console user support, addressing and resolving questions from the sales team
  • Own daily, weekly, and monthly “Run the Business” operations, such as lead and account assignment, data integrity updates, email triaging, and report building
  • Identify areas for improvement, optimize current tasks, and automate manual processes to enhance efficiency and reduce manual work
  • Act as the first line of defense for production support bugs and feature feedback, filing Jira tickets on behalf of the sales team and escalating as needed
  • Maintain comprehensive documentation for all sales processes and Run the Business tasks
  • Learn the “build” side of Sales Ops, assisting with field creation, Flows, page layouts, and list views when possible
  • Assist in new sales tool setup, training, rollout, onboarding, and adoption monitoring
  • Create and maintain standardized reports and dashboards to monitor pipeline health, data integrity, and key performance indicators in Salesforce
  • Support the hygiene and administration of Salesforce through routine data clean-ups and report notifications
  • Execute quarterly projects aimed at elevating sales team efficiency and efficacy
  • Assist in building out Salesforce tools for the New Construction team

What We Look For

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • 1+ years of experience in a Sales Operations capacity
  • Experience using Salesforce
  • Highly detail oriented
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to manage time effectively across multiple work streams and juggle multiple projects
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to thrive in a data-rich environment
  • Experience collaborating effectively with business stakeholders, sales reps, and cross-functional teams
  • Ability to create thorough documentation of work
  • Adhere to all company security policies and data handling procedures.
  • Complete mandatory security awareness training within required timeframes.
  • Promptly report any suspected security incidents or suspicious activity to the Security team.

Salary

  • Base Compensation Range: $76,600 - $100,000/yr
  • 5% annual bonus target, paid quarterly
  • Company equity in the form of RSUs

This is the compensation range for the role in the United States. Actual compensation may vary based on a candidate’s experience, skills, location, internal equity, and evolving business needs. While most offers are generally made within the middle of the range, final compensation is determined based on the factors above.

Benefits

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% employer-paid premiums for employees and their dependents on select plans
    Company HSA, FSA, Dependent Care FSA, 401(k), and commuter benefits
    Employer-paid life and disability insurance
    11 observed holidays and PTO plan

    Continuing education reimbursement

About the role

The Mining Operations Assistant Supervisor plays a critical leadership role in supporting daily field operations, team performance, and installation activities. This primarily field-based position drives productivity, enforces safety standards, and ensures high-quality work. The Assistant Supervisor provides hands-on leadership, coaching, and coordination, serving as a key point of contact for technicians and supporting operational continuity across shifts.

What you'll do

  • Spend about 95% of time in the field supporting technicians, troubleshooting, and keeping operations efficient. Spend 5% on administrative and system tasks.
  • Work alongside technicians to complete daily tasks and meet operational goals.
  • Lead by example through work ethic, safety compliance, and commitment to quality.
  • Drive productivity by ensuring tasks are completed accurately, efficiently, and on schedule.
  • Coordinate daily activities to meet operational priorities.
  • Provide real-time coaching, feedback, and direction to improve team performance.
  • Oversee and take part in end-to-end mining equipment installation: unboxing and installing units, running Cat-5 cables to designated network ports, and modifying materials with hand tools (foam cutting, de-fanning).
  • Ensure installations meet company standards for quality, functionality, and efficiency.
  • Enforce safety policies and regulations, foster a culture of accountability and incident prevention, and promptly identify, address, and escalate safety risks.
  • Safely operate and oversee scissor lifts (up to 20 feet), forklifts, and pallet jacks.
  • Train, coach, and mentor technicians on technical skills, work methods, and safety, from onboarding through ongoing development, while reinforcing performance expectations and accountability.
  • Ensure work orders, priorities, and expectations are clearly communicated and executed.
  • Use OneNote and Microsoft Teams to track progress and share shift pass-downs.
  • Stay aligned with direction from Building Supervisors.
  • Serve as a primary team contact during assigned shifts. Escalate issues when necessary.
  • Lead day/night shift handoffs, including staging materials, tools, and resources for incoming shifts.
  • Ensure operational supplies (e.g., water, ice) and overall shift readiness.
  • Oversee refueling and readiness of company vehicles (e.g., Rangers).
  • Verify tools and equipment are stored, secured, and accounted for at shift end.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, professional workplace by upholding housekeeping and waste disposal standards, overseeing routine cleaning (dusting, sweeping), and confirming workspaces are left in proper condition at shift end.
  • Perform other related responsibilities as assigned to support operational needs and team success.

What you'll bring

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • Prior experience installing computer equipment.  

Physical requirements and work environment

  • Ability to stand, walk, and perform repetitive tasks for extended periods
  • Ability to lift and move equipment as needed (50 pounds)
  • Ability to work onsite in a mining or data center environment (heat, noise, etc.)
  • Exposure to high noise levels and varying temperatures

Safety Requirements

  • PPE & Compliance: Strictly adhere to all site safety protocols and wear required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) at all times (e.g., safety glasses, hearing protection, steel-toed boots).
  • Hazard Awareness: Proactively identify, report, and mitigate potential workplace hazards or unsafe conditions.
  • Standards: Maintain compliance with OSHA regulations and internal safety training.
  • Organization: Keep all work areas clean and free of obstructions to prevent workplace accidents.

Compensation and Benefits 

  • Salary commensurate with experience. 
  • 401(k) retirement plan: Incudes a generous company match.
  • Comprehensive health coverage: Multiple medical plan options, including 100% company-paid plans, HAS & FSA.
  • Work-life balance: Paid time off, sick time and floating holidays.
  • Wellness & lifestyle perks: Enjoy free gym memberships, pet insurance, childcare discounts, employee assistance program, and more to support your life both in and out of work.

Riot is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Lead Mobile Engineer

Europe or United States, remote first with offices available · Full-time · Engineering · Reports to the CTO

About DFNS

Finance is moving onchain. Stablecoins, tokenized deposits, securities and funds are changing how money and assets are issued, held and transferred. The destination is a financial system where any asset can be issued, moved and governed onchain with the controls regulated institutions require. That shift needs a new foundation. Just as core banking systems manage accounts and ledgers today, financial institutions need a platform to manage digital assets. DFNS is that platform. Today, we secure hundreds of billions of dollars in assets every month for more than 500 clients worldwide.

Why this role

Our clients put DFNS in front of their administrators and end users through mobile, where a passkey, a signing approval or a policy decision has to be fast, secure and obvious. You will lead mobile at DFNS, owning the iOS and Android apps and the SDKs clients embed in their own, and bringing fintech UX and bank-level security together on a phone. In year one you will ship the apps our clients rely on, make the SDKs the fastest way to put DFNS inside a client’s app and set the architecture the rest of mobile is built on.

What you’ll do

  • Lead the design and development of our iOS and Android apps, owning features from idea to launch to iteration.

  • Refine the mobile SDKs and cross-platform frameworks clients embed so an integration takes days rather than weeks.

  • Bring fintech UX and bank-level security together on mobile, with WebAuthn, passkeys and secure authentication done right.

  • Set and hold the standards for performance, security and architecture across the mobile stack.

  • Partner with Product and Design to turn complex workflows into simple ones for administrators and end users.

  • Write clear documentation, review code and raise the level of everyone who touches mobile.

  • Work with Product Security so mobile stays a hardened surface rather than the easiest way in.

What you bring

Must-haves

  • A record of leading and shipping production mobile apps in fintech, onchain or another environment where reliability and security were not optional.

  • Expert React Native, with native depth (Swift or Kotlin) for when the framework is not enough.

  • Hands-on experience with WebAuthn, passkeys and secure authentication flows on mobile.

  • Experience building and maintaining SDKs or cross-platform frameworks that other teams integrate.

  • A sharp eye for UX and product detail. You notice the delayed transition and the misaligned button.

  • Ownership of mobile architecture decisions, with the judgment to keep the stack simple.

  • Clear written communication across time zones.

Nice-to-haves

  • Mobile security hardening (jailbreak and root detection, secure storage, certificate pinning).

  • Experience with wallets, key management or signing on device.

  • Design systems and accessibility on mobile.

How we work

We are a distributed company headquartered in Paris. Our teams work from Europe, the US and Asia, with offices in New York, Geneva, Dubai, Singapore, Hong Kong and São Paulo. We write decisions down so they survive time zones. We hold our own work to the standards our clients are held to. We hire people who can own an outcome end to end and we give them the room to do it.

What we offer

A competitive base salary set by role and location, a bonus or variable plan where the role carries one and stock options vesting over four years. Healthcare, flexible vacation, parental leave and a one-time home technology allowance, with travel expenses covered. A MacBook and the equipment you need to do your best work. Remote first, with an office if you want one.

Base salary range: $120,000 to $200,000

Hiring process

We aim to complete the process in 2 weeks and we tell you where you stand after every step.

  • Intro call with Co-CEO (30 minutes).

  • Personality and cognitive assessments, completed on your own time (45 minutes).

  • A technical take-home exercise

  • Focus Interviews (about 2.5 hours): code review (45 minutes), architecture review (45 minutes), cross function (30 minutes) and security best practices (30 minutes).

  • Reference calls and background checks.

Equal opportunity

DFNS is an equal opportunity employer and considers every applicant based on ability and potential, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age or any other characteristic protected by law. If you need an accommodation at any point in the process, tell us and we will arrange it.

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.
OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.

OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About The Opportunity

The Compliance function at OKX is responsible for the overall compliance culture at the company. We're a team of risk-minded problem solvers who advise the business on the company's regulatory obligations and enterprise risk.
The successful candidate will have prior AML transaction monitoring and investigations experience in the financial services, FinTech or cryptocurrency industries. You will help detect unusual activity, suspicious/illegal behaviors and patterns, as well as assist in projects focused on preventing and detecting financial crimes.
As part of the AML Investigations team, you will be responsible for conducting a variety of tasks such as investigations, conducting enhanced due diligence, preparing narrative information for SAR filings, and participating in ad-hoc projects as needed. You will utilize internal and external investigative resources and apply logical research techniques.

  • Conduct thorough investigations on users' account activities as a result of transaction monitoring alerts.
  • Where appropriate, collaborate cross-functionally in the investigation of transaction monitoring cases.
  • Make determinations and recommend escalation decisions on cases investigated.
  • Prepare SAR materials and draft SAR narratives.
  • Conduct research using internal and external sources to help determine potentially suspicious activity and disposition of adverse news
  • Create, update and maintain files and records related to all supporting information used during investigation.
  • Assist with ad hoc projects incl. QA alert dispositions, validation of the transaction monitoring system or any updates, training, etc.

What We Look For In You

  • 3+ years experience in conducting AML-related account activity analysis, due diligence, and investigations in a financial services institution.
  • Strong writing, analytical and communications skills. Must be able to execute tasks within tight deadlines.
  • Strong interpersonal skills are necessary to work effectively with colleagues across regions and business units
  • Should be a self-starter, organized, detail oriented, and results driven
  • Excellent command of spoken and written English is required.

Nice-To-Haves

  • Prior experience working in a multi-national or matrix environment.
  • Knowledge with AML/CFT/Sanctions, money transmission regulations, and industry best practices.
  • Familiarity with commonly used transaction monitoring & reporting tool(s), such as Chainalysis.
  • Relevant industry certifications, e.g. CAMS.
  • Cryptocurrency experience is a plus.

Perks and Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package.
  • Learning and development programs, and education subsidies for employees' growth and development.
  • Team building programs and company events.
  • Wellness and meal allowances.
  • Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants.
  • More that we love to tell you along the process!

This is the first compliance hire for our North American businesses: a Canadian and a US money services business in a regulated payments group. Both businesses are early. They move money across borders for business clients, with foreign exchange where needed, and their volumes are starting now. You will work with a small team and can bring in outside providers for monitoring and reviews, working under your direction. You will report to David.

As Compliance Officer (both entities)

  • Build, then keep current, each entity's written compliance program, with policies approved by a senior officer: client and beneficial-ownership due diligence, enhanced measures for higher-risk clients, record keeping, travel-rule data and training.
  • Assess money laundering, terrorist financing and sanctions-evasion risk across clients, products, delivery channels and geographies, and assess new products, payment rails and corridors before launch.
  • Set the outside compliance provider's scope, review its work and sign off what it produces.
  • Run the written, ongoing training program and its training plan for staff and anyone acting for the entities.
  • Keep each entity's registrations current: the money services business registration with FINTRAC and the payment service provider registration with the Bank of Canada in Canada; the FinCEN registration in the US, renewed every two years and re-filed within 180 days of a triggering change.
  • Lead regulator examinations and requests for information, and answer due-diligence requests from banks, payout partners and clients.
  • Monitor state money transmission licensing requirements for the US entity's activity, and advise the business before it enters a new state or product.

As MLRO (both entities)

  • Run transaction monitoring and sanctions screening, and decide every escalated alert.
  • Canada: file suspicious transaction reports with FINTRAC as soon as practicable after reasonable grounds to suspect are established, and terrorist property reports; oversee the prescribed reports, including international electronic funds transfers and virtual currency receipts of C$10,000 or more.
  • US: file suspicious activity reports with FinCEN for suspicious transactions of US$2,000 or more within 30 days of initial detection, and keep them with their supporting documents for five years; oversee currency transaction reporting and OFAC blocking and reject reporting.
  • Act as the contact for law enforcement requests and production orders, and protect the confidentiality of every report.

As Risk Officer (both entities)

  • Canada: act as the senior officer who oversees the written risk management and incident response framework under the Retail Payment Activities Regulations, its incident reports and its third-party risk, and any safeguarding-of-funds framework if end-user funds are held.
  • Canada: file the annual report to the Bank of Canada by March 31, and give notice of a significant change or new activity at least five business days before it happens.
  • Maintain each entity's risk register and risk appetite, covering compliance, operational, third-party and partner risk, and report it to the board.
  • Commission the independent reviews: FINTRAC's effectiveness review at least every two years, the Bank of Canada framework review at least every three years, and the US program's independent review; track every finding to closure.

Must have

  • At least 7 years in anti-money-laundering and sanctions compliance at money services businesses, payment companies or the payments arm of a bank, including 3 or more as a compliance officer, MLRO or deputy.
  • Deep knowledge of Canada's Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and FINTRAC's guidance, and working knowledge of the Retail Payment Activities Act.
  • Has built a compliance program, not only run one: written its policies, risk assessment and training plan.
  • Has decided on and filed suspicious transaction reports, and has run transaction monitoring and sanctions screening.
  • Has taken a business through a FINTRAC, bank-partner or audit examination and closed the findings.
  • Due diligence on business clients, including clients that pay out for their own customers, and on banks and payout partners.
  • A recognised AML certification, such as CAMS, or equivalent experience.
  • Writes clearly for boards, regulators and banks, and works alone across time zones.
  • Can pass the background checks regulators and banking partners require.

Can be learned here, or nice to have

  • The US Bank Secrecy Act, FinCEN reporting and OFAC sanctions. Specialist support is available while you learn the US regime.
  • Operational risk and incident response frameworks.
  • Cross-border business payments with foreign exchange, or payments funded in stablecoins or other virtual currency, including the travel rule.
  • US state money transmission licensing.
  • Payout corridors in Asia-Pacific.
  • Has managed outsourced compliance providers or set up monitoring and screening tools.
  • Has been the officer of more than one entity at once.

Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Join our Product and Regulatory Legal team, embedded with Kraken's Product, Design and Engineering teams to ship novel products and experiences that accelerate the global adoption of crypto. We are a tight, experienced group of lawyers from a diverse range of tradfi, fintech and crypto backgrounds who move fast, stay curious and take pride in the commercial accountability of our advice, partnering directly with Product, senior leadership and Compliance to chart clear, defensible paths to launch and to keep our licensed entities running smoothly.

This is a senior product-facing legal role for the European Union. You will be the lawyer the business trusts on questions that cut across several regimes at once: for example, a single product such as a tokenised equity, a card, or an institutional custody and prime brokerage service can touch the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive ("MiFID II"), the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation ("MiCA"), the Payment Services Directive ("PSD2"), the Electronic Money Directive ("EMD2") and banking rules at the same time. You will bring clarity on which regime applies, what it requires, and how to launch within it.

 

The opportunity

Reporting to the Head of Product Legal, you will act as a senior legal adviser to European leadership on new products, licensing structure and regulatory strategy.

  • Own cross-functional product counselling for European Union launches from discovery to design, launch and iteration, giving Product, Engineering, Compliance and leadership decision-ready advice with clear options and risk trade-offs

  • Advise on the regulatory perimeter and classification of new offerings across MiFID II and the Markets in Financial Instruments Regulation ("MiFIR"), MiCA, the European Market Infrastructure Regulation ("EMIR"), payment services and electronic money rules, and banking regulation, including where an instrument or service falls between regimes (for example tokenised securities, crypto-asset derivatives, margin and financing, and stablecoin-linked products)

  • Advise on payments and electronic money offerings, including the Krak card and account propositions, safeguarding, open banking and account-access obligations, and the developing Payment Services Directive 3 and Payment Services Regulation framework

  • Advise on banking-related questions that arise in the European Union, including bank partnerships and sponsor-bank arrangements, deposit-taking and lending perimeter questions, the Capital Requirements Regulation and Directive, and the interaction of these rules with our custody, prime brokerage and financing products

  • Monitor and interpret European Union legislative and supervisory developments, take part in consultations and industry association work where appropriate, and translate their significance for the business proactively

  • Draft and negotiate client-facing terms and conditions, taking clear, business-aligned positions

  • Act as gatekeeper for European Union outside counsel engagements: scope the work, estimate and manage cost, and sign off before matters go externally

  • Mentor and develop more junior lawyers in the team, set quality standards for plain-English, risk-based advice, and act as a senior sounding board for colleagues across the Regulatory Legal team

  • Use AI-assisted tools (for example Enterprise GPTs) to speed up regulatory analysis, first drafts and matter tracking, and to build self-service tools that let stakeholders answer commoditised legal and regulatory questions themselves

  • Advise on anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing requirements affecting products, including the Transfer of Funds Regulation ("Travel Rule") and the new European Union anti-money laundering package, and on market abuse, conduct, outsourcing and operational resilience obligations, including the Digital Operational Resilience Act ("DORA")

  • Lead or oversee licensing, authorisation and variation workstreams in the European Union, including scoping requirements, mapping pathways, supervising outside counsel, preparing application materials and managing regulator interactions

 
 

What you bring

  • Qualified lawyer admitted in Ireland, England and Wales, or another European Union Member State

  • 15 or more years' post-qualification experience ("PQE") in financial services regulatory law, gained at a regulated financial services institution (for example a bank, payment institution, broker-dealer, exchange, central counterparty or crypto services provider) or at a leading law firm supporting such clients, ideally with in-house or direct product counselling experience

  • Deep, current knowledge of several of the following, with real depth in at least two: MiFID II and MiFIR (investment services, market structure, derivatives and conduct), MiCA (crypto-asset services, custody, trading platforms and stablecoins), European Union payment services and electronic money regulation, and European Union banking regulation

  • Demonstrated ability to analyse novel products against overlapping regimes and give a clear view on classification and perimeter, including in areas where the rules are unsettled or supervisors have not yet spoken

  • Direct experience managing senior regulator relationships, including notifications, information requests, supervisory correspondence and examinations

  • Working knowledge of anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing, outsourcing and operational resilience obligations, including DORA

  • Proven ability to instruct, supervise and manage the cost of outside counsel across multiple jurisdictions

  • Outstanding analytical, drafting and organisational skills, with crisp, plain-English writing

  • Ability to distill complex legal and regulatory issues into clear, actionable guidance for non-lawyer stakeholders and for senior leadership

  • A pragmatic, commercially accountable approach to legal and regulatory risk that gives stakeholders a useful range of options and a clear recommendation

  • Experience mentoring or managing lawyers, and the judgement to know when to escalate

  • Comfort operating with a high degree of autonomy in a fast-moving, remote environment

  • Familiarity with using AI tools such as Enterprise GPTs to increase the efficiency of legal services

 
 

Nice to haves

  • Experience advising on tokenised securities and the European Union Distributed Ledger Technology Pilot Regime

  • Experience with EMIR, including the clearing obligation, margin for non-centrally cleared derivatives and transaction reporting

  • Experience with prime brokerage, securities financing, margin lending or institutional custody

  • Experience advising on the United Kingdom cryptoasset regime or other non-European Union frameworks that intersect with European Union operations

  • Experience supporting regulatory aspects of corporate transactions, such as change-of-control notifications and entity migrations

  • Experience with European Union data protection and consumer protection rules as they apply to financial products

  • Fluency in a second European language

  • An authentic interest in crypto and digital assets, and familiarity with Payward's and competitors' products
